verdictStatement: Both instances of my v5 SHOULD-FIX are repaired exactly as specified, and both Codex provisionals are repaired in substance at the bytes — which I verified without reading that unfrozen verdict. FC-REPLAY-NAMED no longer expects an undesigned disposition; it now expects a typed fail-closed refusal carrying CONTINUE-REPLAY-NOT-DESIGNED and closes with 'Not an undesigned hole', so the fixture and the row it covers finally say the same thing. FC-RECOVERY-AUTHORITY gains the two vectors the v5 conjuncts lacked, with cardinality and identities still reserved. ceremonyTermination's target is now the toFunction result under the declared meta-target, and a full-text scan finds the token 'computed' surviving only inside explicit denials and attack lines. All five transitions that can refuse for an inactive envelope now carry whenInactive ENVELOPE-INACTIVE, including the ST-TRUSTED EV-INSTALL member that previously would have reported INSTALL-NOT-TRUSTED for an envelope cause, and the two fallback notes that used to claim the inactive case now disclaim it by name. Nothing regressed: the machine is byte-identical to v5 apart from that one transition, the refusal vocabulary is still totally mapped at 13 of 13, and the continuation table still resolves all 343 triples with three permissive outcomes that all require CORE=ST-TRUSTED. The single advisory is a roster parenthetical, and it blocks nothing.

That closes the one path where an envelope-inactive cause would have been reported as INSTALL-NOT-TRUSTED. I enumerated every whenInactive branch in the machine: all five — transitions 0, 1, 2, 3 and 16 — carry ENVELOPE-INACTIVE and nothing else. coordinatorNote: This is an ACCEPT of the artifact, not a disposition of the row, and it carries one scope limit the coordinator should weigh. The Codex v5 verdict exists but is IN-PROGRESS and was not on my read permission list, so I did not read its findings and I do not certify v6's account of CODEX-V5-S1/S2 against that text. What I could do, and did, was verify both claimed repairs directly at the subject's bytes — the 'computed' token is gone from the ceremony record and every inactive-envelope refusal now carries ENVELOPE-INACTIVE — so my acceptance rests on measurement rather than on v6's characterisation of a verdict I have not seen. v6 itself handles that exposure well: it marks the two findings provisional and books the residual in notFoldedThisSuccessor, which is the same field whose false emptiness was a finding against v4. If Codex's frozen verdict turns out to carry anything beyond those two, v6's own note is right that it needs a v7, and this ACCEPT would not cover it. On my side of the ledger nothing is outstanding: both instances of my v5 SHOULD-FIX are repaired as specified, and the only thing I found is a parenthetical. DR-112 remains OPEN, the subject remains CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED / DO-NOT-SEAL / binds NOTHING, and nothing here marks the row SATISFIED or authorizes docs/v2/implementation/.
